title: Optimize Model Performance

header.html: Improve performance by identifying and removing unnecessary rows and columns; Identify poorly performing measures, relationships, and visuals by using Performance Analyzer and DAX query view; Improve performance by reducing granularity
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

toc.title: Reduce granularity and design for speed

html:
1Remove unnecessary rows and columns

An Import model is stored in the VertiPaq engine, which compresses data about 10 times. A smaller model refreshes faster, takes less memory and answers queries faster. The best savings come from loading less data, and you do the work in Power Query so the steps run at the source when they can.

Technique What it does
Remove columns (vertical filtering) Drop every column that no visual, measure or relationship uses
Filter rows (horizontal filtering) Load only the rows you need, such as recent history with a relative date filter or a parameter
Group and summarize Aggregate to a coarser grain, such as one row per day and product instead of one per transaction
Choose data types Numbers compress better with value encoding than text does with hash encoding; fewer distinct values compress better
Custom columns in Power Query Prefer them to DAX calculated columns, which cost more memory
Disable auto date/time Removes a hidden date table for every date column
Disable load for staging queries Clear Enable load on intermediate queries so they are not loaded into the model

A staging query is a query that other queries use as a source. It still runs, but its table is not stored in the model. Keep high-cardinality text, such as free-form comments or unique identifiers that nothing uses, out of the model.

Exam tip

. Vertical filtering removes columns; horizontal filtering removes rows. To shrink a model, filter rows and remove columns in Power Query first. A page or visual filter does not make the model smaller.

Exam tip

. Prefer Power Query custom columns to DAX calculated columns, disable auto date/time, and clear Enable load on staging queries. Numbers compress better than text.

2Performance Analyzer

Performance Analyzer records how long each visual takes to load. In Power BI Desktop, open the Optimize tab and choose Performance analyzer. You can also use it when you edit a report in the service.

Step What you do
1 Open Performance analyzer and choose Start recording
2 Interact with the report, or choose Refresh visuals
3 Choose Stop, then expand each visual to read its durations
4 Use Copy query, Run in DAX query view, or export the log as a JSON file

Each visual logs four durations.

Duration Meaning If it is high
DAX query Time for the model to run the query Tune the measure or the model design, such as relationships
Direct query Time for a DirectQuery source to answer Tune the source, query folding or indexes
Visual display Time to draw the visual Too many data points or a heavy custom visual
Other Time spent on other work, such as waiting for other visuals Too many visuals on one page

Performance Analyzer therefore points to the slow visual, to a slow measure when the DAX query time is high, and to a slow relationship when queries across a bi-directional or many-to-many relationship are slow. Copying the query lets you test it in isolation.

Exam tip

. The four durations are DAX query, Direct query, Visual display and Other. A high DAX query time points to the measure or model, a high Direct query time to the source, and a high Other time to too many visuals.

3DAX query view

DAX query view lets you write and run DAX queries against the semantic model. Open it from the left navigation in Power BI Desktop, or paste a query that you copied from Performance Analyzer.

Item Fact
EVALUATE Required; returns a table as the result
DEFINE Optional; defines measures, variables or columns for this query only
DEFINE MEASURE Lets you test a changed measure without touching the model
Update model with changes Writes the measures you defined into the model
Quick queries Right-click a table or column: show the top 100 rows, column statistics, define all measures
Limits Desktop: 15 MB or 1,000,000 values per query; web: 99,999 rows

A common workflow is to copy the slow query from Performance Analyzer, run it in DAX query view, rewrite the measure in a DEFINE block, and compare the result and the time.

DEFINE
    MEASURE Sales[Total Sales] = SUM ( Sales[Amount] )
EVALUATE
    SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( 'Date'[Year], "Sales", [Total Sales] )
Exam tip

. Every DAX query needs EVALUATE; DEFINE is optional. DEFINE MEASURE changes nothing in the model until you choose Update model with changes.

4Reduce granularity and design for speed

Granularity is the level of detail of a table. Fewer, coarser rows mean less data to scan.

Option What it does
Summary table A table you build at a coarser grain, such as daily instead of per transaction, for visuals that do not need the detail
User-defined aggregation An Import table at a coarser grain, mapped to the detail table with Manage aggregations; queries use it when they can and the detail table otherwise
Automatic aggregations Power BI builds and maintains aggregations for a DirectQuery model for you, based on how reports query it
Hybrid table One table with Import partitions for older data and a DirectQuery partition for the newest data
Dual storage mode A shared dimension that can act as Import or DirectQuery, depending on the query

Model design matters just as much. Use a star schema with one-to-many relationships from dimensions to facts, and avoid bi-directional and many-to-many relationships. Relationships run fastest as one-to-many, then many-to-many through a bridge table, then plain many-to-many, and relationships across source groups are the slowest. Use integer key columns.

Mode Performance
Import Fast: data sits in memory and visuals are fully interactive
DirectQuery Each visual sends queries to the source, so speed depends on the source; needs query folding
Exam tip

. Reduce granularity with summary or aggregation tables, and let hybrid tables or automatic aggregations handle large DirectQuery data. A one-to-many star schema is faster than bi-directional or many-to-many relationships.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A model holds ten years of sales, but the reports use only the last three years. The file is large and refresh is slow. What should you do?

  • AHide the older Date rows from the Report view field list
  • BAdd a page filter for the last three years on each page
  • CCreate a calculated table that keeps the last three years
  • DFilter the rows in Power Query to the last three years
Show the answer

Answer: D. Filtering rows before load shrinks the model, whereas page filters, hidden fields and calculated tables leave the full data in it.

S2In Performance Analyzer one visual shows a long DAX query duration and a short visual display duration. What should you do next?

  • AReduce the data points that the visual draws
  • BRemove other visuals so this one stops waiting
  • CCopy the query and test it in DAX query view
  • DSpeed up the source system's response time
Show the answer

Answer: C. A long DAX query duration points to the measure or the model, and DAX query view lets you test and tune the copied query.

S3A page has 30 visuals. Each visual shows a short DAX query duration but a long Other duration in Performance Analyzer. What is the likely cause?

  • AThe visuals wait for each other to load
  • BThe measures contain slow iterator functions
  • CThe DirectQuery source answers too slowly
  • DThe visuals draw too many data points each
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Other duration includes time spent waiting for other operations such as other visuals, so the page needs fewer visuals.

S4An author wants to test a changed definition of a measure and see the result as a table without editing the model. What should the author write?

  • AA calculated table created in Table view
  • BA quick measure created on the Home tab
  • CA Performance Analyzer recording of the visual
  • DA DEFINE MEASURE block followed by EVALUATE
Show the answer

Answer: D. DAX query view runs a DEFINE MEASURE block with EVALUATE and leaves the model unchanged.

S5A DirectQuery model over a very large sales table is slow on monthly summary visuals. Which change improves the speed the most?

  • AAdd an Import aggregation table at a coarser grain
  • BSet all relationships to filter in both directions
  • CTurn on auto date/time for every date column
  • DChange all the relationships to be many-to-many
Show the answer

Answer: A. An aggregation table answers summary queries from memory and sends only detail queries to the source.

S6Two large tables are joined with a many-to-many relationship that filters in both directions, and visuals are slow. What is the best redesign?

  • AAdd a calculated key column to both of the tables
  • BUse a star schema with one-to-many relationships
  • CTurn on automatic page refresh for the whole report
  • DMove the fact table to DirectQuery storage mode
Show the answer

Answer: B. One-to-many relationships from dimensions to facts are the fastest, and bi-directional many-to-many relationships are the slow case.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are vertical filtering and horizontal filtering?

Show the answer

Removing columns and removing rows.

R2Which setting keeps a staging query out of the model?

Show the answer

Clear Enable load.

R3What are the four Performance Analyzer durations?

Show the answer

DAX query, Direct query, Visual display and Other.

R4Which statement is required in every DAX query?

Show the answer

EVALUATE.

R5Which compresses better, numbers or text?

Show the answer

Numbers, through value encoding.

R6On which tab do you open Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop?

Show the answer

The Optimize tab.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Rows and columns Remove columns (vertical) and filter rows (horizontal) in Power Query; VertiPaq compresses about 10 times
Smaller model Group and summarize, numbers over text, custom columns over calculated columns, auto date/time off, Enable load off for staging
Performance Analyzer Optimize tab; Start recording, interact, Stop; DAX query, Direct query, Visual display, Other
Actions Copy query, Run in DAX query view, export JSON
DAX query view EVALUATE required, DEFINE optional; Update model with changes; quick queries
Granularity Summary tables, user-defined and automatic aggregations, hybrid tables, dual mode
Design Star schema, one-to-many, avoid bi-directional and many-to-many
Storage mode Import is fast; DirectQuery depends on the source and needs query folding
